checks.title: With webRequest and host access to the Directory, onErrorOccurred fires when the stub is stopped, and the tab is replaced by an extension page
checks.observed: Spike extension (host access ["*://go/*","http://localhost:4655/*"], no "tabs" permission), go link while the stub was stopped: onErrorOccurred recorded "net::ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED" for http://localhost:4655/hit/c12-down; chrome.tabs.update replaced the tab with chrome-extension://<spike-extension-id>/unreachable.html?url=http%3A%2F%2Flocalhost%3A4655%2Fhit%2Fc12-down&error=net%3A%3AERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED, which shows "The Directory did not answer", http://localhost:4655/hit/c12-down, net::ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED. At the moment of the error chrome.tabs.get gave url null and pendingUrl null for the tab: it still held the page before (http://thirdparty.example/page, which the extension may not read) and no pending address, so "does the tab show the failed URL" cannot be decided inside the event handler. Retry while still down: 1 more error(s) in 3 s and the tab was on the unreachable page again. Back button, from a tab whose history was http://thirdparty.example/page then the go link: the tab ended on the unreachable page again (1 more error(s); goBack reported "page.goBack: net::ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED"). Typing the Directory's own address (http://localhost:4655/hit/c12-direct): tab replaced. Copy of the extension with host access to ["http://localhost:4655/*"] only, same direct address: recorded "net::ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED" and the tab was replaced. After the stub was restarted, the page's Retry link ended on http://localhost:4655/-/spike/dest.

checks.title: The redirect works with the service worker stopped, and after a browser restart
checks.observed: Spike extension: worker stopped through the DevTools protocol (status "stopped", no worker target), then http://go/ redirected; the navigation woke the worker again (its webRequest listener). After closing and relaunching on the same profile, the first navigation (856 ms after launch) redirected; worker targets at that moment: 1. Its own log over both sessions: ["onInstalled:install: rulePresent false, installedNow true","onInstalled:install: rulePresent true, installedNow false"], so the rule was installed once and found present at the second launch. Rule-only extension (installs the rule once, no webRequest listeners): with the worker stopped http://go/ redirected and the worker stayed stopped; after the relaunch the first navigation redirected, and its lifecycle log ["workerStarted","onInstalled:install","ruleInstalled","workerStarted","onInstalled:install"] shows 1 rule install(s) over both sessions. Control without the extension: page.goto: net::ERR_NAME_NOT_RESOLVED at http://go/hit/c14-control. Go link as the browser's first navigation (Chromium started headless with http://go/... on its command line, on a profile from an earlier session): redirected, the stub logged ["/hit/c14-startup-extension"]; the same start without the extension: stub log [] after 5119 ms. Limits: every launch here loads the extension with --load-extension, which fires onInstalled (reason "install") on each launch and never onStartup, so start-up timing differs from an extension installed the normal way; and a tab restored from the previous session was not tried. The manual run covers the normally installed case (steps L1 to L3).

checks.title: Registering the address-bar keyword go/ leaves a plain go/foo plus Enter unchanged
checks.observed: Default match with spike/extension against spike/extension-omnibox (keyword "go/"), fresh and after a typed visit to http://go/, for "go/foo", "go/", "go/foo/", "http://go/foo", "go": identical in every case. With a space after the keyword the default does change: "go/ foo" (fresh): search-what-you-typed [Search 851 keyword=google.com] -> https://www.google.com/search?q=go%2F+foo&sourceid=chrome&source=chrome.ob&ie=UTF-8 becomes search-other-engine [Keyword 1100 keyword=go/] -> chrome-extension://<spike-extension-omnibox-id>/?q=foo. Keyword hint attached to the default match for: "go/" (fresh), "go/" (after one typed visit to http://go/), "go" (after one typed visit to http://go/), "go/ foo" (after one typed visit to http://go/). Matches the keyword adds, by input, position and relevance: fresh: "go/" at #1 (1100), "go/ foo" at #0 (1100), "go foo" at #9 (450); after one typed visit to http://go/: "go/" at #1 (1100), "go/ foo" at #1 (1100), "go foo" at #9 (450). In keyword mode (after Tab or Space accepts the hint) "go/ foo" gives: fresh: search-other-engine [Keyword 1500 keyword=go/] -> chrome-extension://<spike-extension-omnibox-id>/?q=foo; after one typed visit to http://go/: search-other-engine [Keyword 1500 keyword=go/] -> chrome-extension://<spike-extension-omnibox-id>/?q=foo. PROXY ONLY: this is Chromium's autocomplete code answering through chrome://omnibox in Playwright's headless Chromium, not a person typing in Chrome stable. The manual run must still confirm it.

checks.title: Recorded only: onErrorOccurred with a broad static filter is delivered only for hosts the extension has access to
checks.observed: An extension with host access to http://localhost:4656/* only, and onErrorOccurred registered at the top level with the filter {urls: ["http://*/*", "https://*/*"], types: ["main_frame"]}. Three navigations failed: http://no-access.example/refused (net::ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED), http://no-access-unresolved.invalid/ (net::ERR_NAME_NOT_RESOLVED), http://localhost:4656/granted (net::ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED). Events delivered: [{"error":"net::ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED","url":"http://localhost:4656/granted"}]. Only the host with access was delivered, so a broad static filter does not widen what the extension sees.

checks.title: Proposed check 17: the extension itself can fetch the loopback Directory (the connection test of L4.2)
checks.observed: fetch("http://localhost:4655/-/api/v1/meta") from the extension's status page: HTTP 200 {"product":"godir-spike","version":"0.0.0","api":0}; from its service worker: HTTP 200 {"product":"godir-spike","version":"0.0.0","api":0}. Permission state "local-network-access" as the extension page sees it: "prompt". PROXY ONLY: headless Chromium cannot show a permission prompt, so a fetch that needed one would have failed here; that it worked says no prompt was needed in this build. Chrome stable must confirm it (manual step C3).
